title: Operator Toolsmithing and Runbook Station Design
author: Lena Chen
content:
Overview:

This document codifies a reproducible design for operator workstations (logical and physical), the minimal toolchain for day-to-day incident response, and a template-driven approach to authoring and evolving runbooks. The goal is to reduce cognitive load for oncall operators, accelerate mean time to mitigation (MTTM), and make runbooks verifiable and testable in a lab environment.

Intended audience:
- Platform operators and SREs
- Platform toolsmiths and platform UX engineers
- Oncall rotations and operator apprentices
- Playbook maintainers and runbook authors

Outcomes and success metrics (6 months):
- MTTM reduction of 25% for severity-2 incidents involving inference routing (baseline Q2-2025).
- 80% of operator runbooks have automated verification tests in the synthetic lab.
- Operator satisfaction (internal survey) ≥ 4.0/5 for workstation tooling.

Design principles:
- Toolsmithing first: build small utilities that codify operator heuristics into reliable scripts and UI helpers.
- Observable-by-default: every tool must emit structured telemetry and a correlation ID for traceability.
- Local reproducibility: runbook steps should be runnable in the operator sandbox (no production changes required).
- Minimal cognitive surface: default commands and dashboards show actionable signals, not raw telemetry.
- Auditability: every manual remediation step should be recorded (CLI wrapper or web UI) for post-incident review.

Operator Runbook Station (ORS) components:
1) ORS shell (cli-ors) - lightweight CLI wrapper that:
   - exposes common remediation commands (drain, evict, rotate-model, restart-router).
   - records actions to the operator-events stream with correlation_id.
   - integrates with SSO and short-lived credentials.
2) ORS dashboard - a small web UI showing prioritized alarms, suggested runbooks, and granular telemetry slices.
3) Sandbox lab - ephemeral environment for validating runbooks and CLI commands against synthetic traces.
4) Runbook repository - canonical markdown + metadata for every runbook and automated validators.
5) Telemetry hooks - standard fields and event types used by ORS components (see Telemetry section).

Runbook authoring template (must be used for new and updated runbooks):
- Title
- Summary (1–2 lines)
- Impacted services and owners
- SLOs and thresholds that trigger this runbook
- Prerequisites (access, credentials, sandbox steps)
- Readable step-by-step remediation (numbered)
- CLI commands and CLI flags with examples
- Safety checks and preconditions (automated gates)
- Validation steps (how to confirm mitigation)
- Rollback procedure
- Postmortem checklist items

Example runbook (shortened):
Title: Evict misbehaving model worker (evict-model-worker)
Summary: Use when a model worker is producing 5xx errors for >3 minutes and network/infra checks are green.
Impacted services: runtime-proxy, kv-cache, model-scheduler
SLO trigger: 5xx-rate > 5% over 5m for route /v1/generate
Prerequisites:
- Operator role with project:runtime:evict permission
- cli-ors installed and authenticated
Steps:
1. Correlate alerts: cli-ors list-alerts --route /v1/generate --last 10m --corr-id ${CORR}
2. Check worker health: cli-ors check-worker --id <worker-id>
3. Mark worker drained: cli-ors set-state --id <worker-id> --state DRAINING --note "Investigating 5xx"
4. Evict from pool (safe-evict flow): cli-ors evict-worker --id <worker-id> --grace-period 30s --dry-run && cli-ors evict-worker --id <worker-id>
5. Validate: cli-ors tail-metrics --route /v1/generate --window 2m | grep "5xx-rate"
Rollback: cli-ors set-state --id <worker-id> --state ACTIVE --note "rollback due to false-positive"

Runbook metadata table (Confluence pipe table - copy into pages):
| Field | Example value | Required? | Notes |
| Title | evict-model-worker | yes | Short, hyphenated id for automation |
| severity | sev2 | yes | Severity this runbook addresses |
| owners | eng-platform/ops | yes | Team alias |
| validated | yes/no | yes | Indicates if lab tests exist |

Telemetry contract (minimum fields emitted by all ORS tools):
- correlation_id: uuid
- operator: <email>
- tool: cli-ors|ors-dashboard|runbook-validator
- action: evict-worker|set-state|restart-router|prefetch-prime
- target_type: worker|pool|route
- target_id: string
- before_state: string
- after_state: string
- result: success|failure
- duration_ms: integer
- trace_id: optional (link to tracing system)

Example telemetry JSON (emit as a single line JSON to operator-events):
{
  "correlation_id": "d7f3b8c2-4a6e-4b56-9a9a-1bc2f8e2a0de",
  "operator": "lena.chen@redwood.ai",
  "tool": "cli-ors",
  "action": "evict-worker",
  "target_type": "worker",
  "target_id": "worker-42",
  "before_state": "ACTIVE",
  "after_state": "EVICTED",
  "result": "success",
  "duration_ms": 1432
}

Operator sandbox (lab) guide - quickstart:
1) Provision: labctl create --profile operator-sandbox --ttl 2h --tags {"purpose":"runbook-test"}
2) Seed workload: labctl seed --scenario inference-5xx --routes /v1/generate --qps 20
3) Run runbook steps with dry-run flags: cli-ors evict-worker --id worker-42 --dry-run
4) Verify with telemetry replay: labctl replay-trace --corr-id <corr> --inspect
5) Destroy: labctl destroy --id <sandbox-id>

Deployment and rollout plan for ORS (3 phases):
Phase 1 (Q1 2026) - Tooling and Runbook Templates
- Deliver cli-ors v0.1 with audit events and SSO auth.
- Publish 12 canonical runbooks with lab validation.
- Train two oncall cohorts (workshops).
Acceptance criteria: 12 runbooks validated, cli-ors emits telemetry to operator-events, workshop feedback > 3.8/5.

Phase 2 (Q2 2026) - Dashboard and Operator UX
- Launch ORS dashboard v0.1 (limited to eng-platform oncall).
- Integrate suggested runbook linking and one-click dry-run of safe commands.
- Add automated gates for high-risk commands (requires two-operator confirmation).
Acceptance criteria: Dashboard used in 40% of rotations, two-operator confirmation works end-to-end.

Phase 3 (Q3 2026) - Automation and Metrics
- Add runbook-verifier that runs nightly synthetic tests and reports coverage.
- Add cost and latency signals to suggested action heuristics.
- Onboard other platform teams (infra, runtime) for cross-team runbook sharing.
Acceptance criteria: 80% runbook coverage in lab, MTTM reduction goal on track.

Safety and compliance checklist for operator actions:
- All actions require operator-events emission and link to an incident (if severity ≥2).
- High-impact actions (evict, model-swap) require TOTP confirmation and operator role check.
- Changes are reversible: every runbook must include a rollback path tested in lab.

Training and certification path (operator toolsmithing):
- Self-study: read runbook templates and complete two lab exercises (evict, prefetech-prime).
- Workshop: 4-hour hands-on with senior operator (mentor).
- Certification: pass practical exam in the synthetic lab (provision, remediate, validate)

Maintenance and ownership:
- Ownership: eng-platform/tools owns cli-ors and runbook-validator.
- Runbooks: authorship is the team that owns the service; eng-platform/playbooks maintains templates and audits compliance quarterly.
- Telemetry schema changes must be backward-compatible and coordinated with observability-team.

Post-incident workflow (short):
1) Incident commander assigns correlation_id and tags the incident in the incident tracker.
2) Operator executes runbook via cli-ors (audit recorded).
3) If further escalation required, record decision and update incident timeline.
4) After resolution, runbook events are replayed in the lab to validate and capture any gaps.

Appendix A — Minimal ORS CLI API (examples):
- cli-ors auth login --sso
- cli-ors list-alerts --route /v1/generate --last 10m
- cli-ors check-worker --id worker-42 --json
- cli-ors set-state --id worker-42 --state DRAINING --note "Investigating 5xx"
- cli-ors evict-worker --id worker-42 --grace-period 30s --dry-run
- cli-ors tail-metrics --route /v1/generate --window 2m

Appendix B — Example runbook-validator job (YAML):
job_name: runbook-validator-evict
schedule: nightly
inputs: [evict-model-worker]
steps:
  - provision_sandbox: true
  - seed_traffic: inference-5xx
  - run_runbook_dry_run: cli-ors evict-worker --id {{worker_id}} --dry-run
  - run_runbook: cli-ors evict-worker --id {{worker_id}}
  - validate: check 5xx-rate < 1% within 5m
  - teardown: true

Appendix C — Frequently asked questions (short):
Q: What if my runbook has no rollback?
A: Mark it as high-risk and schedule a lab validation before merging. We do not allow production-only irreversible steps without two-operator signoff.

Q: How do I get operator access for sandbox tests?
A: Request the "operator-sandbox" role via self-service (internal IAM portal). The role grants temporary credentials with TTL by default.
